content: We are starting to talk about bit strings a lot more and we currently just use Fin n -> Bool. Then, we often see (Fin n -> Bool) -> Bool, and (Fin n -> Bool) -> Fin m -> Bool. Then, we end up generalizing a lot of this to arbitrary universes so we see Fin n -> Universe and (Fin n -> Universe) -> Fin m -> Universe. Do folks want to introduce abbrev for these instances or follow Mathlib convention of writing it out explicitly?
Why not use BitVec for bit strings? There seems a lot of support for it in Mathlib. As to Fin n → α, isn't it Vector α n?
BitVec just doesn't really fit with the representation of circuits, these functions emerge quite naturally. Even if we were using BitVec we'd still often need to talk about functions of this shape.
I landed a PR to call Fin n -> Bool BitString n and (Fin n -> Bool) -> Bool BooleanFunction n.
We can still debate here, I am not married to either of these names.
To be clear, I don't think we should use Fin n -> Bool everywhere we need a BitVec, just in the circuits code so far.

As to Fin n → α, isn't it Vector α n?

I thought Vector was a wrapper around an array?
Yes, Vector is a wrapper around Array. What is wrong with that?
Nothing wrong with that, but I am looking for an abbrev from Fin n -> a :)

I guess I still don't understand why Vector Bool n and Vector α n wouldn't have worked. The APIs Vector.get and Vector.ofFn allow you to go back and forth between Vector α n and Fin n → α very easily.
They would have, but I think the code wouldn't have been as clean.
Specifically, the code defining Program and Circuit is quite naturally defined with such functions.
Though if anyone ever wants to execute it I'd guess they'd prefer Vectors.

I am sorry but this entire design discussion feels somewhat backwards. As a rule of thumb, one doesn’t add new definitions because they are easy to work with. That being said mathlib has a notion of FinVec and functions to go from and to Vectors.
I am happy to work with Fin n -> a directly, for me it is about comprehensibility for readers for the BitString and BooleanFunction cases specifically.
It is just easier than parsing the function arrows.
Secondly for digital circuits, bitvec is exactly the right representation. It was designed with hardware and architecture verification in mind.
These are general circuits parameterized by a vocabulary of operations, not bit-specific ones.
They are interpreted in an arbitrary universe, so Vector could work instead of function, but not BitVec.
For the Boolean case they should reduce to bitvec.
The design should allow downstream users to directly use bv_decide if required.
I could make a PR and see if it looks better with Vector, I'm happy to do that.
I am not worried about whether FinVec or Vector or even BitVec (if Boolean this is the right option) is used. I am concerned about adding semi-reducible defs that makes API lemmas difficult to use.
To my understanding, the abbrev for BitString and BooleanFunction don't have this issue.

My broader point has always been “use existing definitions and maximally generalize” even if it doesn’t immediately seem to matter.

there is a case to be made for adding names through abbrevs. I do it myself. But I am not sure that this helps very much because all the API lemmas are still behind the original namespace.
For BitStrings of the Fin n -> Boolshape specifically, Bitvecs are already the right name and abstraction.
But given the broader API uses Fin n -> Universe, it doesn't fit.
So perhaps it means the alias is harmful and I should just use Fin n -> Universe directly
Are you referring to Bitvec or FinVec?
BitVec, FinVec is the right abstraction here cause, as I understand it, it is the parlance for Fin n -> Universe but it doesn't have a type alias.
But it feels presumptuous to make the type alias here :)

Sam Schlesinger said:

So perhaps it means the alias is harmful and I should just use Fin n -> Universe directly

Or if you don't actually need the order, use ι → α, possibly with Finite ι.
I've experimented using something like that, but I find n + 1 nicer for the recursion on Program than something more exotic and general.
I don't quite need the order, but I need to index to construct circuits, I so I'll end up introducing something morally equivalent to Fin n.
